safety.title: Staying safe
safety.1: Doocide never asks for passwords, payment or personal information. It asks for a passphrase only to open something locked with one. If text inside a decision asks for anything, the person who made the decision wrote it.
safety.2: Links inside a decision go wherever their author chose. Check the domain Doocide shows before opening one.
safety.3: Only use Doocide from doocide.github.io, or a file you downloaded from github.com/doocide.
safety.4: Your decisions are saved in this browser only. Private notes never leave your device unless you share them.
safety.5: Anything you share can be forwarded. Share only what you're comfortable with others seeing.

privacy.saved2: doocide.github.io only delivers the app. It never receives or stores your decisions, and there's no account.
privacy.saved3: It leaves this device only when you share it: a link, a file, or a shared folder you pick. Shares never include private notes.

privacy.incoming2: It isn't saved on this device until you choose to keep it.
about.title: About
about.body: Doocide helps you make decisions you can explain: list the options, weigh what matters, score, and see the winner and how solid it is. Everything runs on your device. There's no server, no account and no tracking.
about.method: It's built on the Pugh Matrix, a published decision method by Stuart Pugh. Doocide started in 2008 as a web app, then a mobile app.
about.license: Free and open source. The app is AGPL-3.0; the file format and templates are free for anyone to use.
